analysis_steps.goal: Extract the HCN (3-2) spectrum and measure hyperfine component ratios

method.value: Collapse spectrum over all channels in a 3x3 arcsec area; compare B/A and C/A ratios with the optically thin LTE expectation (0.04)

evidence.quote: the observed HCN (3-2) spectrum collapsed over all velocity channels and measured over an area of 3x3 arcsecond that covers the full spatial scale of the observed structures
Under optically thin LTE conditions, the relative weightings of the HCN (3-2) hyperfine lines are 0.037:0.926:0.037.
measured over an area of 3x3 arcsecond that covers the full spatial scale of the observed structures

assumptions.value: LTE level populations proportional to statistical weights give B/A = C/A = 0.04

evidence.quote: assuming that the level populations of the hyperfine states are in LTE and hence proportional to the statistical weights.

validation.value: Anomaly checked against radiative transfer model, which reproduces ratios of ~0.05 before abundance changes

evidence.quote: The line radiative transfer model originally produces B/A and C/A hyperfine intensity ratios in HCN of $\sim$0.05, which is close to the LTE value of 0.04.

restricting the fit to a region excluding the filamentary (or spiral) structure.

findings_qualitative.value: HCN-A emission shows an extended spiral from the proto-brown dwarf position, with a compact bar-like peak close to the continuum peak

findings_qualitative.value: HCN survives in the gas phase in the dense core center while HCO+ is centrally depleted

evidence.quote: There is an enhancement in the HCN abundance towards the core center, which suggests that HCN can survive in the gas phase in the inner, dense regions of the proto-brown dwarf.
In contrast, modelling of the HCO$^{+}$ (3-2) line emission indicates that it originates from the outer pseudo-disk/envelope region and is centrally depleted.

claims.hypothesis: HCN (3-2) can trace the inner Keplerian disk of a Class 0 proto-brown dwarf
claims.experiment: Mapped HCN (3-2) at ~0.4 arcsec, fit the bar-like peak, and compared with non-LTE radiative transfer models of an MHD simulation
claims.result: Compact bar-like peak of ~50 au near the continuum peak, reproduced by the model as the inner dense region; no velocity gradient found in moment 9
claims.finding: Bar likely traces the inner disk, but Keplerian kinematics cannot be confirmed with the present velocity resolution

evidence.quote: Radiative transfer modelling indicates that the bar-like structure is tracing the inner disk, albeit confirming the Keplerian kinematics will require at least $\sim$10 times higher velocity resolution than the present observations.
The non-detection of Keplerian rotation in the bar-like structure is thus mainly due to the limited velocity resolution of the observations.

claims.hypothesis: The HCN hyperfine line ratios deviate from optically thin LTE values
claims.experiment: Measured B/A and C/A ratios from the collapsed spectrum and compared with the LTE value and with radiative transfer models including hyperfine splitting
claims.result: B/A and C/A ~0.2 versus 0.04 in LTE; model initially gives ~0.05
claims.finding: The hyperfine anomalies are real and likely reflect different hyperfine components tracing different physical regions, not one single effect

evidence.quote: Therefore, based on the modelling results, we can say that the hyperfine line ratios are truly anomalous.
Such anomalies cannot be pinpointed to one particular effect.

claims.hypothesis: The extended spiral in HCN traces the pseudo-disk/envelope
claims.experiment: Compared observed moment maps with the best-fit model moment maps
claims.result: Model reproduces the spiral for a 30 deg misalignment and 60 deg inclination
claims.finding: The spiral traces a pseudo-disk twisted by core rotation

evidence.quote: The spiral-shaped structure is tracing the pseudo-disk that has been twisted due to core rotation.

claims.hypothesis: HCN and HCO+ probe different regions, with HCN surviving and HCO+ depleted at the core center
claims.experiment: Modelled both lines with the same physical model and compared their moment 0 maps, peak offsets and spectra
claims.result: HCN peaks ~66 au and HCO+ ~176 au from the continuum position; HCN abundance enhanced and HCO+ depleted toward the center in the models
claims.finding: HCN reveals small-scale structure in regions where HCO+ is depleted

evidence.quote: Based on the modelling results, HCN can trace the innermost, densest regions in the proto-brown dwarf where HCO$^{+}$ is depleted from the gas phase.

why_this_data.value: Disks of <=10 au expected in brown dwarfs are hard to resolve, so a high-density tracer is used to probe the innermost regions

evidence.quote: An alternative way is to use high-density molecular line tracers that can probe the innermost densest regions in compact, dense proto-brown dwarfs.

why_this_method.value: Moment 8 chosen over moment 0 to show where the spectral peak originates for the bar

evidence.quote: we want to highlight the region of origin of the peak or maximum value of the spectrum, due to which moment 8 is preferred over moment 0 map.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Moment 1 map not used for kinematics because no velocity gradient is seen, so moment 9 is shown instead

evidence.quote: Since there is no velocity gradient seen within the spiral or bar structures, the moment 1 map does not show any velocity fields.

limitations_admitted.value: Limited velocity resolution prevents confirming Keplerian rotation or building a PVD

evidence.quote: The non-detection of Keplerian rotation in the bar-like structure is thus mainly due to the limited velocity resolution of the observations.
Thus, velocity dispersions of $<$0.6-0.8 km s$^{-1}$ cannot be resolved.

limitations_admitted.value: Bar and spiral are separated visually by an intensity cut

evidence.quote: The distinction between the spiral and bar features is made visually.

limitations_admitted.value: HCN B and C components only barely detected, so the bar is not visible there

evidence.quote: These fainter components are barely detected at a $\sim$3-$\sigma$ level compared to A that is detected at a $>$10-$\sigma$ level.

referee_caveats_inferred: The bar-as-inner-disk interpretation rests on a modified MHD simulation and a model-by-eye comparison; no uncertainties on best-fit model parameters and no alternative physical models are tested
Kinematics unconstrained: no rotation signature detected, so the Keplerian disk claim is not observationally confirmed
Offset of the bar from the continuum peak (~44 au) and the 60 deg viewing angle are used to explain asymmetric emission without independent test
Gas mass and density derivation (excitation temperature, HCN abundance, optical depth) is not described
Single source, single data set, with bar and spiral separation done visually
